prospect.name: Istvan
prospect.location: A small town near Budapest, Hungary
prospect.occupation: Export sales manager at a large manufacturer of high-voltage grid transformers; desk-bound, sitting eight to nine hours a day plus commuting, which he estimates at ten hours of sitting daily
prospect.family_status: Married with three small children; wife bought him his first kettlebells
prospect.training_background: Played sports throughout his life and started weight training around 14-15, but describes it as hobby level. Did almost nothing for roughly the last five to ten years because of children and work. Recently returned to calisthenics at home, then bought kettlebells about two months ago after seeing short-form videos, and now trains three to four times a week at 5:30am for about an hour using a 12 kg bell. Says the plastic-framed kettlebells his wife bought online have unusable handles and need replacing.
prospect.medical: Sacroiliac and lowest lumbar joint pain for about a year, rated 6-7 out of 10 at its worst and worst on waking - 'the crossbones and all those joints there hurt like hell.' He has not seen a clinician about it: 'I have to go to the doctor probably.' He has self-researched the condition and believes it needs stretches and medical training rather than kettlebells. Also reports increasing general stiffness after previously being flexible, and lactose intolerance diagnosed roughly twenty years ago.

signals: Explicitly good-to-great: 'I'm not overweighted, I don't want to lose weight actually... I'm okay-shaped, I don't have to lose. But gaining muscle, yeah, exactly.'
Price met no resistance of any kind - the only issue was that his money sits in savings and it was the end of the month
Already executing at a high standard before buying: three to four sessions a week at 5:30am for two months, and seeing results
Buying refinement rather than rescue - form correction, progression, measurable feedback: 'after a limit or a level, it's hard to have a progress alone, because there's no checkup, no feedback'
Cuts against the classification: a year of untreated 6-7/10 spinal pain, which is closer to the_medically_constrained than the taxonomy allows for someone with no price resistance

goals.text: Gain a few kilos of muscle, especially in the legs and core rather than only the upper body
Not look weak, thin or old - a lifelong self-image issue since being a skinny teenager
Move more freely and agilely, without stiffness, and run up stairs without issues
Reduce or manage the lower back and sacroiliac pain, though he doubts kettlebells alone will do it
Extend healthy lifespan by holding on to muscle mass as he ages
Have kettlebells as a genuine hobby, which he says he otherwise lacks
Be someone his three children see training and are a little proud of
Learn correct technique and get objective feedback so progress does not stall

pains.text: Sacroiliac and low lumbar joint pain for about a year at 6-7 out of 10, worst on waking, never assessed by a clinician
Sits roughly ten hours a day between desk work and commuting, and is losing flexibility he used to have
Did almost no training for about five years because three small children, work and household left no time for himself
Lifelong self-image as a skinny, weak-looking man - 'I don't want to look, you know, weak and old and thin'
Progress plateaus training alone with no form check, no feedback and no way to verify technique
Protein intake almost certainly too low for muscle gain and not tracked at all
Lactose intolerance rules out dairy protein sources
Losing muscle and gaining fat with age and needs to reverse it

notable.note: The most serious clinical finding in the batch. The prospect disclosed a year of 6-7/10 sacroiliac and low lumbar joint pain and said in plain terms that he has not seen a doctor about it. He then correctly reasoned that kettlebells would not fix it and that he needs stretching and medical treatment - and the rep talked him out of that position using Trevor's own injury story and a specific claim about a named client called Lou whose back hernia pain supposedly dropped from six or seven to three or four, before promising 'eventually the pain does get less.' The sale followed. Separately, the rep twice stated on the record that he is not permitted to book an onboarding meeting inside twelve hours and booked one anyway: 'Usually I'm not allowed to book that, but I don't care.'
